findings.title: Blanket delete of past reminders removes cancelled reminders before they are cancelled in SendGrid
findings.body: The existing `deleteMany` removes every EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate is in the past. It runs before the new cancel step, so those rows never reach it. The cancel query only picks up cancelled reminders scheduled within the next hour. Cancelled reminders that sit in the 1-72h window and are only picked up later are fine. But a cron run that is skipped or delayed past the send time deletes the row and the email still goes out. The delete also doesn't touch the SendGrid batch. The cancel step should run before this cleanup, or the cleanup should skip rows with cancelled=true.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and orphan rows are never cleaned
findings.body: All cancel requests share a single try/catch. If one `client.request` throws (for example the 100 pending-cancellation limit, or a bad batch id), the loop exits. The remaining cancelled reminders are skipped for that run, and the prisma deletes collected in the array are never awaited, so even the already-cancelled rows are not removed. The array of deletes is also built lazily and awaited only at the end, so a failure loses them. The failure is only logged. The cancel and delete should be handled per reminder inside the loop.

findings.title: Cancel query is not limited to EMAIL and null referenceId is not excluded
findings.body: `findMany` filters only on cancelled and scheduledDate. It does not filter on method=EMAIL or on referenceId being non-null. Cancelled rows with a null referenceId would send `batch_id: null` to SendGrid. This cron also never calls `client.setApiKey`. That is done in emailReminderManager, which this file doesn't import, so the request may be unauthenticated depending on module load order.

findings.title: Rescheduled/cancelled reminders scheduled less than an hour out can still be sent
findings.body: Non-immediate deletion only sets cancelled=true. The cron runs every 15 minutes but only cancels reminders within the next hour. The reminder time is not checked here, so a reminder scheduled in under an hour is only cancelled on the next cron run. Because the row is not deleted and the cancel is deferred, a window remains where the email is still sent. Also, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is not awaited by callers, so failures are silent.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget reminder deletion races with attendee/booking deletes
findings.body: The `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls are neither awaited nor included in `Promise.all`. The SMS delete removes the row by id with no existing check. The bookings' reminders may also be cascade-deleted concurrently, so the delete can throw and is swallowed by the catch. The process can also end before the calls finish (serverless), leaving the reminders uncancelled.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row
findings.body: With immediateDelete=true the SendGrid cancel is sent but the workflowReminder row is not deleted or marked cancelled. For the workflow-delete path the cascade covers it. For the reschedule path in handleNewBooking the row is left behind, uncancelled, with scheduled=true. The cron later deletes it once its date passes, but the semantics are inconsistent.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace changes in commented-out code
findings.body: The diff strips indentation inside the commented-out testAction block, which adds noise. The `Prisma` import is also now a value import that is unused.
